results.title: Peterborough Court taps Freshwave for all-operator mobile coverage
results.description:
What was once the famous, architecturally imposing former home of Telegraph newspapers in London has now made a full transformation into a modern media hub. As part of the redevelopment, connectivity infrastructure-as-a-service provider Freshwave is bringing all-operator mobile connectivity to the new Peterborough Court.

Built in the 1880s and located in the old heart of the UK’s newspaper industry, Fleet Street, and still popularly known as the Telegraph Building, Peterborough Court has undergone a complete redevelopment to create high-spec grade A office space while retaining its art deco façade.

The office space spans more than 300,000 sq ft across 11 floors and has stated aim of having a focus on wellbeing through the creation of outdoor spaces, on-site amenities and “state-of-the-art end-of-trip” facilities. It has terraces on four floors and boasts panoramic views of London. Peterborough Court’s sustainability credentials include a WiredScore Platinum rating, a target BREEAM “Excellent” or better rating, and an all-electric design that is said to reduce significantly whole life carbon.

Also high among the key features of the space are “diverse telecoms intake rooms and diverse risers”. Advanced communications is an essential element of the building and, in this regard, Freshwave believes that mobile connectivity is no longer an add-on for commercial buildings.

Working with commercial property IT and smart building infrastructure specialists TCM, Freshwave has deployed its small cell Omni Network with all the mobile network operators throughout the landlord areas.

The firms regard Peterborough Court as an prime example of how digital infrastructure is becoming a defining feature of premium commercial real estate. Connectivity was treated as a core building service from the outset, ensuring occupiers benefit from what is claimed to be reliable, high-performance mobile coverage alongside the wider smart building infrastructure.

Tenants are able to opt into extending the service to their workspaces through a pay-as-you-occupy model, with Freshwave providing support through their ongoing managed service.

“Peterborough Court represents exactly the kind of premium workspace that today’s occupiers are looking for. We’ve seen strong demand for the building and are pleased that all-operator mobile connectivity is one of the many amenities that we will be offering to occupiers,” said Jason Gallehawk, associate director at CBRE, the joint leasing agent for the building.

“Omni Network’s lower energy use made it a natural choice, as sustainability was at the heart of this redevelopment, while still offering the same reliable, seamless coverage across all operators that tenants expect from a best-in-class London workspace.”

Freshwave senior director Brendan Hourihane added: “We’re delighted to be working with CBRE and TCM to bring assured connectivity into Peterborough Court. With building materials and low-e glass blocking mobile signal from entering from outside, Omni Network extends all the mobile networks indoors so that everyone inside receives the capacity they need.

“We’re already seeing good uptake of the service from tenants who are moving into the building and look forward to working with more of them in the future as space in this fantastic building is snapped up.”

TCM managing director Tom McAuley said: “We’re proud to have worked with Freshwave to deliver a future-ready solution that supports both the current and long-term needs of the building and its tenants.”

results.title: Over 2,300 H1N1 cases among 3,000 influenza infections in Delhi; CM calls for emergency meeting
results.description: In light of increasing influenza cases, Delhi's Chief Minister Rekha Gupta convened an emergency review meeting. Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh reassured citizens that all necessary resources are available to combat the issue. The city has reported around 3,000 influenza cases this year, with 2,308 cases linked specifically to H1N1. Hospitals have set up isolation wards to treat affected patients, emphasizing that there is no reason for public alarm.
